correctness.rationale: For a two-state generator with exit-rate sum s, write \(Q=-s(I-\Pi)\) with stochastic rank-one projector \(\Pi\). One midpoint half-step is \(\Pi+r(I-\Pi)\), where \(r=(1-hs/4)/(1+hs/4)\); squaring replaces r by \(r^2\in[0,1]\), so every entry is nonnegative for all h and row sums stay one. For the three-state pure-birth generator, exact multiplication gives endpoint entry \(R_{12}=16h(4-h)/(h+4)^3\), while all other entries are nonnegative; therefore positivity holds exactly for \(0\le h\le4\) and fails for every larger h. Independent matrix replay reproduced the transition matrices and sign change.

value.rationale: The result isolates a sharp low-dimensional exception hidden by class-wide SSP theory: two-state Markov dynamics are endpoint-immune at arbitrary steps, while one extra state is enough to realize the global radius sharply. This is a meaningful minimal-dimension boundary for positivity-preserving time integration.

final_claim: For the two-stage SSP-optimal SDIRK2(2) method, equivalently two implicit-midpoint half steps, every two-state continuous-time Markov generator has a nonnegative stochastic endpoint matrix for every step size, whereas the three-state pure-birth generator already loses endpoint positivity exactly beyond \(h=4\); hence three states are minimal for endpoint failure and the SSP radius four is sharp inside three-state CTMCs.
limitations: The claim is endpoint positivity only; internal RK stages need not be nonnegative beyond the SSP restriction.
